artifact.title: A Q-minus-Q-squared product pair gives the pure projected repair and cancels Cartan backreaction
artifact.status: exact spectral-weight identity and product cancellation
artifact.question: Can the pure projected repair be generated by ordinary product commutators while cancelling the positive Cartan q^2 mass?

finiteIdentity.premise: Q is Hermitian with Q^3=Q, so its eigenvalues are +1,-1,0 and Q^2 is the support projector.
finiteIdentity.eigenvalueProof: For an entry D_ij, the right side has weight (lambda_i-lambda_j)^2-(lambda_i^2-lambda_j^2)^2: it is 4 only for (+1,-1) pairs and zero for support-boundary, same-sign, and zero-zero pairs.
finiteIdentity.positivity: Although written as a difference of two norms, the combined finite quadratic form is positive semidefinite on every D when Q^3=Q.

productConstruction.action: Delta V=c sum_{s=L,R}{||[D,N tensor Q_s]||^2-||[D,N tensor Q_s^2]||^2}.
productConstruction.reality: The L and R contributions are paired by J as in v534.
productConstruction.mixed: Every Cartan-finite mixed term vanishes separately by the Clifford trace audit.
productConstruction.finiteReduction: The spin trace factor 4 gives Delta V_finite=16c P(D), the pure projected ray kappa_U=0.
productConstruction.result: The spacetime Cartan/coframe q^2 term cancels exactly while the positive A-B finite repair remains.

coefficientTarget.matching: With the normalization Delta V_finite=16c P, the minimal coefficient is c>=9/400 in the dimensionless convention where the v519 repair coefficient is kappa_P.
coefficientTarget.caveat: Physical mass scales and normalized traces must be restored before interpreting c numerically.

significance: This removes boundary leakage, so the minimal delta=9/25 threshold is sufficient.
It removes the +176/ell^2 Cartan mass that destabilized a soft Q in v527.
It uses only Q and its polynomial support Q^2; no independent projector or auxiliary Hilbert doublet is required.
It makes an exactly constrained/fixed central partial involution the most economical current branch.
risks: The second product norm appears with a negative coefficient before the partial-involution identity is imposed; an action principle must justify the combined positive finite form rather than treating the terms independently.
If Q varies in spacetime or departs from Q^3=Q, derivative and radial sectors need not remain positive and Cartan cancellation need not hold.
Heat-kernel/spectral actions with positive test functions may not generate the required relative minus sign.
Gauge or gravitational fluctuations outside the factored background could spoil the simple cancellation.
falsifiers: Direct matrix evaluation finds a D entry for which the finite difference is negative under Q^3=Q.
The product action forces separate positivity of the Q and Q^2 invariants and forbids their relative minus.
The exact calculus introduces cross terms between the two invariants that re-create boundary leakage.
Q^4 differs from Q^2 in the operative representation or under quantum corrections.
next: Seek a single supertrace, inclusion-exclusion, or Möbius projector formula that produces the norm difference without a hand-set negative coupling.
Audit the identity for arbitrary complex matrices on all 44 robust carriers.
Test small violations Q^3-Q and quantify the first unstable correction.
Derive the paired difference from an auxiliary-field completion with a bounded total action.
artifact.conclusion: The constrained central branch has an exact product-geometric realization with unusually good economy: a Q minus Q^2 commutator pair is globally positive on finite fields, selects only A-B links, and cancels its own Cartan mass. Its remaining hard problem is the origin and stability of the relative minus sign.

artifact.title: The Q-minus-Q-squared action has no open positivity neighborhood around the partial-involution locus
artifact.question: Is the positive projected difference stable when Q fluctuates slightly away from Q^3=Q?

entrywiseFormula.general: For Hermitian Q eigenvalues lambda_i,lambda_j, the coefficient of |D_ij|^2 in ||[Q,D]||^2-||[Q^2,D]||^2 is w_ij=(lambda_i-lambda_j)^2[1-(lambda_i+lambda_j)^2].
entrywiseFormula.positivity: The difference is nonnegative for arbitrary D iff |lambda_i+lambda_j|<=1 for every pair connected by an admitted D entry.
entrywiseFormula.exactLocus: At lambda in {+1,-1,0}, opposite signs have weight 4, support-zero pairs have weight 0, and all other pairs have weight 0.

perturbations.plusBoundary: Positivity near (+,0) requires u+z<=0 to first order.
perturbations.minusBoundary: Positivity near (-,0) requires v+z>=0 to first order.
perturbations.implication: Generic unconstrained perturbations include both signs and immediately create negative boundary directions; the exact locus lies on the boundary of the positivity cone.

symmetricRadial.range: The difference is nonnegative only for |q|<=1.
symmetricRadial.belowOne: For 0<|q|<1 it is positive but develops boundary leakage, so it moves off the pure projected ray.
symmetricRadial.aboveOne: For |q|>1 boundary directions have negative quadratic weight.

implications: The 440 random-matrix positivity audit in v536 relies essentially on exact Q^3=Q.
A merely stiff soft potential cannot guarantee boundedness of the relative-minus action under local Q fluctuations.
The cancellation construction is safest when Q is fixed/discrete or enforced by an exact nonlinear constraint.
If Q must be dynamical, the directly sandwiched norm ||Q^2[Q,D]Q^2||^2 remains manifestly positive but its derivation from the product commutator pair is lost away from the constraint.
falsifiers: The physical calculus forbids all support-zero D entries, removing the dangerous boundary pairs.
Additional positive invariants dominate the negative weights for every allowed Q fluctuation.
A nonlinear parametrization enforces |lambda_i+lambda_j|<=1 identically while retaining the desired dynamics.
Quantum corrections preserve Q^3=Q as an operator identity rather than a potential minimum.
next: Build a bounded auxiliary-field completion whose elimination yields the relative-minus form only on the constrained branch.
Classify nonlinear parametrizations of a central partial involution with no radial modes.
Compute the minimum positive boundary counterterm needed for a specified fluctuation radius.
artifact.conclusion: The elegant Cartan-cancelling difference is not robust to generic soft-Q fluctuations: exact partial-involution kinematics is a structural requirement. The constrained central/discrete interpretation is therefore strengthened again.

artifact.title: A Z2 odd-character projector gives the pure A-B repair as one manifestly positive norm
artifact.question: Can the projected repair be generated without treating a relative minus between two norm squares as fundamental?

construction.support: S=Q^2 for an exact Hermitian partial involution Q^3=Q.
construction.z2Action: On the supported operator space SDS, conjugation alpha(D)=QDQ satisfies alpha^2=1.
projectorProperties: Both are orthogonal for the Hilbert-Schmidt operator inner product.

exactSelector.eigenvalueAction: For lambda_i,lambda_j in {+1,-1} on support, Pi_- multiplies D_ij by [1-lambda_i lambda_j]/2.
exactSelector.result: Pi_- keeps exactly opposite-sign A-B entries and kills A-A, B-B, and every support-zero entry.
exactSelector.normDifferenceRelation: It also equals 1/4[||[Q,D]||^2-||[Q^2,D]||^2], but positivity is now primary rather than inferred from a subtraction.

productUse.spinEmbedding: Multiplying Pi_- by the algebraic Clifford factor B=gamma_*N gives a product operator with positive spin norm but no derivative [D_M,N].
productUse.cartanBackreaction: No Cartan q^2 mass is generated by this filtered finite term because it is not obtained from the full commutator [D,N tensor Q].
productUse.threshold: kappa_P>=9/25 gives the already proven global radial closure with zero boundary leakage.

interpretation: The repair is the odd sector of a finite Z2 conjugation, making the discrete-order interpretation of Q operational rather than cosmetic.
This supplies a manifestly positive action principle for the same selector that v535 expressed by inclusion-exclusion.
The cost is that spacetime Cartan dynamics and finite filtering are no longer forced to arise from one undifferentiated product commutator.
A conditional expectation or finite-group spectral action is now a more promising derivation target than a positive heat-kernel polynomial of a single C.
advantages: Exact on every representation carrying the same central partial involution.
falsifiers: The admitted action calculus cannot contain operator-space conditional expectations or Z2 character projections.
Q conjugation fails to preserve the supported finite one-form space.
KO6/J completion maps the odd projector to an inequivalent sector with cancelling sign.
Quantum corrections destroy the exact partial-involution relation.
next: Verify that Pi_- maps the exact represented one-form space into itself.
Derive Pi_- from averaging over a discrete gauge group or crossed-product algebra.
Audit J Pi_-^L J^-1=Pi_-^R and the grading signs explicitly.
Compare normalized coefficients with the product commutator formulation.
artifact.conclusion: The pure projected repair is exactly the squared norm of the Z2-odd component of the supported finite Dirac operator. This is positive by construction and avoids both the relative-minus instability and the product Cartan mass, at the price of adopting a discrete conditional-expectation action.

artifact.title: A J-paired two-invariant sum realizes the full product repair without fermion doubling
artifact.status: exact reformulation and preferred minimal product ansatz
artifact.question: Can the side-doublet bookkeeping be replaced by an action on the original finite Hilbert space?

construction.originalHilbert: Use the existing H_S tensor H_F, with no auxiliary C^2 multiplicity.
construction.reality: J_F exchanges Q_L and Q_R, so product J exchanges the two summands and their equal-coefficient sum is J-invariant.

exact_reduction.mixed: Each summand has zero Cartan-finite mixed trace by the v521-v522 Clifford audit.
exact_reduction.cartan: The covariantly contracted Cartan pieces give 16c[Tr(Q_L^2)+Tr(Q_R^2)]q^2/ell^2=2816c q^2/ell^2.
exact_reduction.equivalence: These are exactly the coefficients obtained from the unnormalized side-doublet trace.
exact_reduction.multiplicity: No fermion state or Dirac eigenvalue is duplicated.

interpretation: The auxiliary side doublet of v523/v533 is a convenient direct-sum notation, not a required physical degree of freedom.
Reality naturally motivates equal left and right coefficients because J exchanges the two invariants.
The product repair can therefore remain on the preferred 184-dimensional finite carrier.
The positive q^2 sign lock and relative factor 176/ell^2 from v527 remain unchanged.
artifact.qualification_to_v533: The fermion-doubling obstruction applies only if the direct-sum side representation is promoted to the physical spectral Hilbert space. It is absent for the J-paired action sum.
falsifiers: The action principle permits only one single-trace compensator insertion and forbids a J-paired sum of invariant norms.
KO6 completion gives the two exchanged terms opposite rather than equal coefficients.
Left/right commutators are not separately admitted one-forms in the exact quotient calculus.
A nonzero cross term between the two action summands is compulsory and changes selectivity.
next: Derive the paired sum from a real spectral action or symmetrization prescription rather than postulate equal coefficients.
Audit whether radiative corrections can split the left and right coefficients despite J.
Repeat the product calculation with the projected Q^2[Q,D]Q^2 operator.
artifact.conclusion: The full unrestricted A-B repair needs no auxiliary physical doublet. A J-exchanged pair of product-compensator invariants on the original Hilbert space gives the same finite and Cartan coefficients and removes the fermion-doubling concern.
